name: Hanoi French Hospital (nearest international-standard hospital)

price: Not verified
tip: The nearest international-standard hospital, in Hanoi about 100 km away (1.5-2 hours by expressway). Switchboard 024 3577 1100. Ninh Binh has no international hospital. For a serious case, call 115 and the provincial hospital switchboard first for coordination — do not drive the long distance yourself before you are stable.

name: Ninh Van Stone Carving Village
address: Xuan Vu Village, Ninh Van Commune, Hoa Lu District, Ninh Binh Province
price: Free to wander; small carved souvenirs priced by the workshop — ask before buying
hours: Not verified — a working village, best visited in daytime
tip: Small statues and animal figures travel best; large pieces are made to order for temples and gardens. Combine it with a bike ride from Tam Coc — it is close enough to cycle.

name: Van Lam Embroidery Village
address: Ninh Hai Commune, Hoa Lu District, Ninh Binh Province (Tam Coc-Bich Dong tourist area)
price: Not verified — priced by the piece; scarves are the affordable end, framed pictures cost more
hours: Not verified — a working village, best visited in daytime
tip: If a "hand-embroidered" scarf costs less than a bowl of pho, it is machine-made. Pay the real price and you are paying the artisan, not a factory.

name: Half-Day Cooking Class at a Local Home (Tam Coc Queen Travel)
address: Hotel pickup in Tam Coc or Ninh Binh City; the exact family-home address is shared after booking
price: From about $32 per person (about 832,000 VND); cheaper private classes in Tam Coc start from about 380,000 VND (~$15) per person for 2 hours — see https://ninhbinhcookingclass.com
tip: Book at https://www.getyourguide.com/ninh-binh-l1232/ninh-binh-half-day-cooking-class-at-a-local-home-t984987/ — free cancellation up to 24 hours in advance. Wear clothes you do not mind getting muddy; the farm activities are real, not a demonstration.

name: Hanoi Railway Station
address: 120 Le Duan Street, Hoan Kiem District, Hanoi
price: Train berth to Lao Cai from about 475,000 VND (~$18)
hours: Not verified — check the timetable at the station or on dsvn.vn
tip: Overnight trains leave late evening; arrive at the station 30 minutes early.

name: Lao Cai Railway Station
address: Hoang Lien Street, Lao Cai City, Lao Cai Province
price: Shared van to Sa Pa about 60,000–100,000 VND (~$2–4)
tip: Shared vans wait outside the station for each arriving train; agree the price before boarding.

name: Fansipan Mountain (Sun World Fansipan Legend)
address: Hoang Lien Station, Muong Hoa Valley, about 3 km from Sa Pa town centre, Lao Cai Province
price: Cable car return: adult 850,000 VND (~$33), child 1–1.4 m 550,000 VND (~$21), under 1 m free. Muong Hoa mountain train return: 200,000 VND (~$8). Full journey with both funiculars: 1,370,000 VND (~$53) adult. Saturday and holiday cable car tickets may be 900,000 VND (~$35).
hours: Not verified — published hours vary by source (around 7:30–17:00); check on the day, and check for maintenance closures before you plan around it.
tip: Go only on a clear morning. If the summit is in cloud from town, save your money for another day — the view is the whole point. The cable car takes about 15 minutes; from the top station it is a climb of about 600 steps to the 3,143 m summit marker, or take the summit funicular.

name: Cat Cat Village
address: Cat Cat Village, San Sa Ho Commune, about 2–3 km south-west of Sa Pa town, Lao Cai Province
price: Adult 150,000 VND (~$6), child 1–1.3 m 70,000 VND (~$3), under 1 m free. Cash at the gate.
hours: About 6:00–18:00 daily (sources vary slightly; ticket sales end in the late afternoon)
tip: The easiest village walk from town — downhill all the way, 2–3 hours with the waterfall and craft stalls. It is the most touristy village, so treat it as a warm-up, not the real thing. Buy tickets only at the official gate and ignore sellers on the road outside.

name: Muong Hoa Valley (Lao Chai – Ta Van)
address: Muong Hoa Valley, Lao Chai and Ta Van villages, about 8–10 km south-east of Sa Pa town, Lao Cai Province
price: Valley entrance fee 75,000 VND (~$3) per adult
tip: This is the classic Sa Pa trek: rice terraces, a river, Black Hmong villages at Lao Chai and Giay villages at Ta Van. Allow a full day on foot, or half a day by motorbike with stops. Best light is early morning, when mist sits in the valley, and late afternoon, when the terraces turn gold in September.

name: Sa Pa Stone Church
address: Hoang Lien Street, Sa Pa town centre, Lao Cai Province
price: Free
tip: The town's meeting point. On Saturday evenings the square in front fills with local people and a small market — good for photos and people-watching.

name: Love Waterfall and Silver Waterfall (Thac Tinh Yeu & Thac Bac)
address: Hoang Lien National Park, National Highway 4D, about 12–15 km north-west of Sa Pa town, Lao Cai Province
price: Not verified — check at the park gate
tip: Two roadside waterfalls on the way to Tram Ton Pass. Love Waterfall needs a short forest walk; Silver Waterfall is visible from the road. Combine both with the pass viewpoint in one half-day by motorbike or taxi.

name: Tram Ton Pass (O Quy Ho Pass)
address: National Highway 4D, about 15–18 km north-west of Sa Pa town, on the Lao Cai–Lai Chau border, Lao Cai Province
price: Free to stop at the viewpoint; taxi one way about 150,000–200,000 VND (~$6–8)
tip: Vietnam's highest mountain road pass, with a famous viewpoint locals call Heaven's Gate. Best at sunset on a clear day. It is cold and windy up here even in summer — bring a jacket.

name: The Hill Station Signature Restaurant
address: Not verified — please check on Google Maps
tip: A reliable upmarket pick in the town centre for Hmong-inspired dishes and good wine. Book ahead on weekends.

name: Red Dao Restaurant
address: Not verified — please check on Google Maps
price: Mains roughly 80,000–200,000 VND (~$3–8)
tip: Popular with travellers for salmon hotpot and grilled dishes. Go early — it fills up by 19:00.

name: Sa Pa Night Market
address: Near the Stone Church square, Sa Pa town centre, Lao Cai Province
price: Street snacks 20,000–60,000 VND (~$1–2)
tip: Best for grilled skewers, corn and sticky rice. Eat where locals are queuing, and carry small notes.

name: Hotel de la Coupole – MGallery
address: 1 Hoang Lien Street, Sa Pa town centre, Lao Cai Province
price: High-end; from about 3,500,000 VND (~$135) per night (check at booking — prices vary by season)
tip: The town's grandest hotel, in a French-colonial style building on the main street. Best for a splurge or honeymoon.

name: Sapa Jade Hill Resort & Spa
address: Not verified — please check on Google Maps
price: Mid-range to high-end; roughly 1,500,000–3,000,000 VND (~$58–115) per night (check at booking)
tip: Hillside bungalows with valley views, a short drive from the centre. Ask for a valley-facing room.

name: Ta Van Homestay area (valley homestays)
address: Ta Van Village, Muong Hoa Valley, Sa Pa, Lao Cai Province
price: Budget; roughly 200,000–500,000 VND (~$8–19) per person per night including dinner and breakfast at many family homestays
tip: Book through a trekking company so the family expects you. Rooms are simple — a mattress, blankets and a shared bathroom — but the welcome is warm. Bring a warm layer: valley nights are cold.

name: Sa Pa General Hospital
address: Not verified — please check on Google Maps
price: Not verified
tip: For anything serious, the nearest well-equipped international-standard hospitals are in Hanoi, about 5–6 hours away. Carry travel insurance that covers mountain evacuation.

name: Sapa O'Chau — Head Office, Cafe & Hmong Showroom
address: 8 Thac Bac Road, Sa Pa Town, Lao Cai Province
price: Brocade scarves about 100,000–300,000 VND (~$4–12); bags and jackets cost more
tip: A social enterprise run by H'Mong people — the most reliable place in town for authentic, maker-made brocade. The cafe upstairs is a good meeting point for treks.

name: Sa Pa Night Market
address: Luong Dinh Cua Street, Sa Pa Town, Lao Cai Province
price: Dried buffalo meat about 50,000–70,000 VND (~$2–3) per 100 g; brocade and silver jewellery priced at the stall
hours: Opens around 6:30 PM; closing time not verified
tip: The easiest one-stop souvenir shop in town: smoked meats, dried fruit, forest honey, tao meo wine, brocade and silver. Taste the free samples before you buy, and haggle gently. Most of the goods here are mass-produced, so save serious brocade shopping for the village workshops or the O'Chau showroom.

name: Cat Cat Village
address: Cat Cat Village, San Sa Ho Commune, about 2–3 km south-west of Sa Pa town, Lao Cai Province
price: 150,000 VND (~$6) per adult; 70,000 VND (~$3) for children 1–1.3 m; free for children under 1 m
hours: Not verified — sources disagree (6:30 AM–6:00 PM vs 6:00 AM–9:00 PM)
tip: Walk down from town (30–45 minutes, downhill) and take a motorbike taxi back up — the return climb is steep. Buy tickets only at the official gate and ignore sellers on the road outside.

name: Ta Phin Village
address: Ta Phin Commune, about 12 km north-east of Sa Pa town, Lao Cai Province
price: Free to enter the village; Red Dao herbal bath about 150,000–200,000 VND (~$6–8)
hours: Not verified — an open village with no gate or fixed hours
tip: Go with a local guide — the village is spread out, and a guide knows which houses welcome visitors and sell genuine embroidery. Ask before photographing people.

name: Ta Van Village (valley homestays)
address: Ta Van Village, Muong Hoa Valley, about 8–10 km south-east of Sa Pa town, Lao Cai Province
price: Homestays roughly 200,000–500,000 VND (~$8–19) per person per night including dinner and breakfast; full-day guided trek roughly 500,000–800,000 VND (~$19–31) including lunch
tip: Stay in the valley rather than town if you want to wake up in the terraces. Book ahead for September–November weekends, and withdraw cash in town first.

name: Dong Hoi Airport (VDH)
address: Loc Ninh Commune, Dong Hoi City, Quang Tri Province (formerly Quang Binh)
price: Taxi to Phong Nha town 400,000–625,000 VND (~$15–24)
tip: Arrange your transfer before you land — taxis are available but the homestay shuttle is usually cheaper and waiting for you.

name: Dong Hoi Railway Station
address: Dong Hoi City, Quang Tri Province (formerly Quang Binh)
price: Taxi to Phong Nha town 400,000–625,000 VND (~$15–24)
tip: The B4 bus leaves from Dong Hoi bus station, about 1.5 km from here — ask station staff to point you to it.

name: Paradise Cave (Dong Thien Duong)
address: Paradise Cave, Phong Nha-Ke Bang National Park, about 30 minutes' drive from Phong Nha town, Quang Tri Province
price: Entry about 250,000 VND (~$10) per adult; some sources list 270,000 VND (~$10) including the electric buggy. Buggy separately about 60,000 VND (~$2) return. Children 1.1–1.3 m about 125,000 VND (~$5); under 1.1 m free.
tip: The show-stopper. Discovered in 2005, it runs for more than 30 km, but visitors walk about the first kilometre on a wooden boardwalk through enormous chambers of glittering stalactites. Go when it opens or after 14:00, when the tour groups have moved on. Allow 2.5 hours including the walk or buggy ride from the car park.

name: Phong Nha Cave
address: Phong Nha Cave boat station, Son River, Phong Nha town, Quang Tri Province
price: Entry 150,000 VND (~$6) per person plus a shared boat — the boat costs about 550,000 VND (~$21) split between up to 12 people (sources list 360,000–700,000 VND for the boat, so check the board). Children under 1.3 m free.
tip: The classic: a boat ride up the Son River and into a cave of still water and pale formations. Allow about 2 hours. Go early to share a boat quickly — if you arrive alone, you wait until enough people gather or pay for the whole boat yourself. Closed when the river floods, usually October–November.

name: Dark Cave (Hang Toi) & Chay River
address: Chay River, about 20 minutes from Phong Nha town, Phong Nha-Ke Bang National Park, Quang Tri Province
price: Full package about 450,000 VND (~$17) per adult including zipline, kayaking, cave walk and mud bath; some sources list 350,000 VND (~$13) for a shorter package. Check at the counter.
hours: Not verified — daytime only; check on the day
tip: The fun one: a 400 m zipline across the Chay River to the cave entrance, then a swim into the dark with a head torch and a wade through a chamber of warm mud. Allow about 3–4 hours. You must weigh over 40 kg for the zipline. Wear clothes you do not mind ruining, and bring a change of clothes.

name: Tien Son Cave
address: Above Phong Nha Cave, Son River, Phong Nha town, Quang Tri Province
price: Entry about 80,000 VND (~$3) per adult
tip: A dry cave above Phong Nha Cave, reached by a steep climb of several hundred steps. Quieter than its famous neighbour, and the view over the river from the entrance is lovely. Often combined with the Phong Nha Cave boat trip.

name: Son Doong Cave (expedition only)
address: Deep inside Phong Nha-Ke Bang National Park; expeditions depart from Phong Nha town, Quang Tri Province
price: About 80,000,000 VND (~$3,000) per person for the 4–6 day expedition with Oxalis Adventure, the only licensed operator. Includes park fees, guides, porters, meals and camping gear.
hours: Expeditions run January to August only
tip: The largest cave in the world, with its own jungle and clouds inside. Only about 1,000 permits are issued a year, and places sell out 12–18 months ahead — new bookings start in 2028. You cannot visit independently, and any operator other than Oxalis claiming to offer it is not legitimate. If Son Doong is out of reach, Hang En (below) gives you much of the same magic for a tenth of the price.

name: Hang En Cave (Oxalis expedition)
address: Phong Nha-Ke Bang National Park; expeditions depart from Phong Nha town, Quang Tri Province
price: About 9,500,000 VND (~$365) per person for the 2-day, 1-night trek with Oxalis Adventure
hours: Trips run December to around August or mid-September
tip: The world's third-largest cave, where you camp on a sandy beach inside the cave itself, under a shaft of light from the jungle above. Moderate fitness required; ages 16–70. Book 2–6 months ahead.

name: Bamboo Cafe
address: Not verified — please check on Google Maps
price: Mains roughly 60,000–150,000 VND (~$2–6)
tip: A long-running traveller favourite on the main street for Vietnamese dishes, good coffee and a relaxed garden. A good first dinner after a long travel day.

name: Phong Nha Farmstay Restaurant
address: Not verified — please check on Google Maps
price: Mains roughly 80,000–200,000 VND (~$3–8); set family dinners roughly 150,000–250,000 VND (~$6–10) per person
tip: Set dinners are served family-style on the veranda overlooking the fields — book in the morning so the kitchen can prepare.

name: Phong Nha Town Morning Market
address: Phong Nha town centre, near the Son River bridge, Quang Tri Province
price: Breakfast dishes 20,000–50,000 VND (~$1–2)
tip: Come for pho, sticky rice and strong Vietnamese coffee, and to watch the town wake up before the tour buses arrive.

name: Phong Nha Farmstay
address: Not verified — please check on Google Maps
price: Mid-range; roughly 800,000–1,500,000 VND (~$31–58) per night (check at booking)
tip: One of the original farmstays, with a pool, gardens and a restaurant. A good base for families and first-timers.

name: Easy Tiger Hostel
address: Not verified — please check on Google Maps
price: Budget; dorm beds roughly 150,000–250,000 VND (~$6–10), private rooms roughly 400,000–800,000 VND (~$15–31) (check at booking)
tip: The social hub for backpackers — bar, pool, and help booking every cave and trek in the park. Book ahead in the February–April high season, when prices rise 20–40%.

name: Chay Lap Farmstay
address: Not verified — please check on Google Maps
price: Mid-range; roughly 1,000,000–2,000,000 VND (~$38–77) per night (check at booking)
tip: Riverside farmstay near Dark Cave, with kayaking and a farm restaurant. Good if you want to be close to the Chay River activities rather than in town.

name: Quang Binh General Hospital (Dong Hoi)
address: Not verified — please check on Google Maps
price: Not verified
tip: The nearest major hospital is in Dong Hoi, about 45–60 minutes by road. Phong Nha town has only a small health station for minor issues. For anything serious, go to Dong Hoi, and for international-standard care, Hue or Hanoi. Carry travel insurance that covers adventure activities and evacuation.

name: Phong Nha Market
address: Main street near the Phong Nha–Ke Bang Tourist Center, Son Trach Commune, Bo Trach District, Quang Binh Province
price: Not verified — check at the stall; khoai deo, honey and rice paper are all inexpensive market goods
hours: Not verified — busiest 6:00–9:00 AM; many stalls close around 11:00 AM and reopen in the afternoon
tip: Go in the morning, when the market is liveliest and the dried goods are freshest. Bring cash and a reusable bag.

name: Oxalis Home Boutique
address: Phong Nha Commune, Son Trach Village, Bo Trach District, Quang Binh Province
price: Not verified — check in the shop
tip: The boutique inside Oxalis Home, run by the cave-tour company. The best place in town for cave pearls and limestone jewellery — the one souvenir you cannot buy anywhere else.

name: Phu Bai International Airport
address: Phu Bai Ward, Huong Thuy Town, Hue City (about 14–15 km south of the centre)
price: Taxi to the city centre about 190,000 VND (~$7.30) — older source, confirm with the driver. Airport minibus about 50,000 VND (~$1.90) — older source, not recently verified.
hours: Open daily from early morning to late evening
tip: Agree the taxi price before you get in, or book a Grab. The minibus drops off at the main hotels — ask the driver if yours is on the route.

name: Hue Railway Station
address: 2 Bui Thi Xuan Street, Hue City
price: Hue–Da Nang train 100,000–250,000 VND (~$4–10)
hours: Open daily from early morning to late evening (ticket office about 07:30–19:30)
tip: The station is a handsome French colonial building from 1906. Book the daytime SE19/SE20 services for the Hai Van Pass views.

name: Hue Imperial City (Dai Noi / The Citadel)
address: 23 Thang 8 Street, Hue City (enter through Ngo Mon Gate)
price: Adult 200,000 VND (~$7.70); children 7–12: 40,000 VND (~$1.50); under 7 free. Combo tickets (valid 2 days): Citadel + 2 tombs 420,000 VND (~$16); Citadel + 3 tombs 530,000 VND (~$20). Audio guide 150,000 VND (~$5.80).
hours: Summer (16 March–15 October) ticket sales 06:30–17:30, site closes about 18:30; winter (16 October–15 March) ticket sales 07:00–17:00, site closes about 18:00
tip: The Citadel is huge — allow at least 3 hours, and come early for the changing of the guard at Ngo Mon Gate around 08:00. The Thai Hoa Palace restoration was completed in 2025 and is open again. E-tickets are available at eticket.hueworldheritage.org.vn. The combo ticket is the best value if you plan to visit the tombs.

name: Tomb of Tu Duc
address: 7/69 Le Ngo Cat Street, Thuy Xuan Ward, Hue City (about 5 km from the centre)
price: Adult 150,000 VND (~$5.80); children 7–12: 30,000 VND (~$1.15); under 7 free. Included in the Citadel combo tickets.
tip: The most romantic of the tombs — a lakeside garden of pavilions, pine trees and lotus ponds, built by the emperor for himself in 1867. Go in the late afternoon, when the light is golden and the crowds have gone.

name: Tomb of Minh Mang
address: Huong Tho Commune, Huong Tra Town, Hue City (about 12 km from the centre, on National Highway 49)
price: Adult 150,000 VND (~$5.80); children 7–12: 30,000 VND (~$1.15); under 7 free. Included in the Citadel combo tickets.
tip: The most formal and symmetrical of the tombs — a straight axis of courtyards, lakes and pavilions built in 1840–1843. The bridge over the lake to the emperor's burial mound is the classic photo.

name: Tomb of Khai Dinh
address: Thuy Bang Commune, Huong Thuy Town, Hue City (about 10 km from the centre)
price: Adult 150,000 VND (~$5.80); children 7–12: 30,000 VND (~$1.15); under 7 free. Included in the Citadel combo tickets.
tip: The most unusual tomb — a steep climb to a concrete palace covered in glass and porcelain mosaics, part Vietnamese, part French, part Art Deco. The interior is dark and glittering; it is worth the climb.

name: Thien Mu Pagoda
address: Ha Khe Hill, Kim Long Road, Kim Long Ward, Hue City (about 5 km west of the centre, on the Perfume River)
price: Free (donations welcome)
tip: Hue's unofficial symbol — the seven-storey Phuoc Duyen tower, built in 1601, on a pine-covered hill above the river. Come in the early morning for the quiet, or at sunset. Dress modestly; this is an active pagoda.

name: Perfume River Dragon Boat
address: Toa Kham Boat Station, Le Loi Street, Hue City
price: Not verified — agree the price before boarding; private boats and group tours are sold at the pier and by hotels
tip: The classic Hue experience: a slow dragon boat up the river to Thien Mu Pagoda (30–45 minutes each way). Sunset cruises are the prettiest. Agree the price, the duration and whether the return is included before you step on board.

name: Dong Ba Market
address: 2 Tran Hung Dao Street, Hue City
price: Free to enter; bargain for souvenirs and fabric
tip: Hue's biggest market since 1899 — food, fabric, conical hats and souvenirs under one roof. The food stalls at the back are a good place to try Hue's small cakes (banh beo, banh khoai) for a few thousand dong each.

name: Bun Bo Me Keo
address: 20 Bach Dang Street, Hue City
hours: 07:00–10:00 daily (mornings only — when the pot runs out, it closes)
tip: The most famous bun bo Hue in the city, and a morning-only affair. Come early, order a bowl with everything, and eat it the way the regulars do: fast, hot, and with plenty of fresh herbs.

name: Quan Cam (Bun Bo Hue)
address: 45 Le Loi Street, Hue City
tip: Phone: +84 234 3931 762. A reliable all-day option for bun bo Hue on the main riverfront street — good when you miss the morning-only shops.

name: Com Hen Ba Cam
address: 34 Le Loi Street, Hue City
tip: Com hen — rice with tiny river clams, peanuts, herbs and a spoonful of chilli — is Hue's working-class lunch. It is salty, spicy and addictive. Ask for "it cay" (less spicy) if you are not used to Hue chilli.

name: Banh Khoai Lac Thien
address: 35 Le Loi Street, Hue City
price: Not verified
tip: Banh khoai is Hue's crispy pancake — smaller and thicker than the southern banh xeo, filled with pork and shrimp. Eat it with the peanut dipping sauce, and order the banh beo (tiny steamed rice cakes) on the side.

name: Banh Beo Ba Cam
address: 10 Le Loi Street, Hue City
price: Not verified
tip: Banh beo are delicate little steamed rice cakes topped with dried shrimp and crackling, served in stacks of small dishes. A proper Hue snack — order two plates, not one.

name: Lien Hoa Vegetarian Restaurant
address: 3 Le Quy Don Street, Hue City
price: Not verified
tip: Hue has a strong Buddhist vegetarian tradition, and this is one of the city's best-known vegetarian restaurants. The vegetarian bun bo Hue is a revelation — ask for it by name.

name: Azerai La Residence Hue
address: 5 Le Loi Street, Hue City
price: Not verified — check on Agoda or Booking.com
tip: High-end, in a restored 1930s colonial mansion on the river — the most atmospheric stay in Hue, and the pool looks out over the Perfume River. (Note: some older listings give 26 Le Loi; the correct address is 5 Le Loi.)

name: Hue Central Hospital
address: 16 Le Loi Street, Hue City
price: Not verified
tip: Phone: 0234 3822 325. This is the city's main hospital, right on the hotel street. For international-standard care, ask your hotel about the International Medical Center (3 Ngo Quyen Street, phone 0234 3890 888).

name: Thuy Xuan Incense Village
address: Huyen Tran Cong Chua Street, Thuy Xuan Ward, Hue City (incense shops cluster around 62-84 Huyen Tran Cong Chua Street)
price: Free to visit; incense bundles priced by the shop — ask before buying
hours: Not verified — a working village street, best in the morning when the incense is laid out to dry
tip: Go in the morning for the best light on the coloured incense and the fewest tour groups. Ask before photographing inside a family's workshop — a small purchase is the polite thank-you.

name: Phu Cam Conical Hat Village
address: South bank of the An Cuu River, Phuoc Vinh Ward, Hue City
price: Poem hats about 150,000-500,000 VND (~$6-19); ordinary conical hats much less
hours: Not verified — a working village, best visited in daytime
tip: Hold the hat up to the light before you buy — that is how you check the hidden poem is really there. A poem hat with no poem visible in sunlight is not a poem hat, whatever the price.

name: Da Nang International Airport
address: Hoa Thuan Tay Ward, Hai Chau District, Da Nang
price: Grab to the city centre 50,000–90,000 VND (~$2–3.50); metered taxi 60,000–150,000 VND (~$2.30–5.80), plus a small airport exit fee of 10,000–15,000 VND (~$0.40–0.60)
tip: Ride-hailing pick-up is in a designated zone about 50 m from the arrivals hall — follow the signs instead of taking the first taxi that approaches you inside the terminal.

name: Da Nang Railway Station
address: 791 Hai Phong Street, Thanh Khe District, Da Nang (main gate at 200 Hai Phong Street)
price: Da Nang–Hue train 100,000–250,000 VND (~$4–10)
hours: Open daily from early morning to late evening
tip: Book the daytime SE19/SE20 services for the Hai Van Pass views; night trains pass the coast in the dark.

name: Ba Na Hills & the Golden Bridge
address: Ba Na Hills, Hoa Ninh Commune, Hoa Vang District, Da Nang (about 25 km west of the city centre)
price: Cable-car ticket about 950,000–1,000,000 VND (~$37–38) per adult; children 1–1.4 m about 750,000–800,000 VND (~$29–31); under 1 m free. Da Nang residents pay less. Combo ticket with lunch buffet about 1,250,000–1,300,000 VND (~$48–50). Prices vary by source — check at the ticket counter.
hours: Cable car 08:00–22:00 daily; Golden Bridge area 08:00–18:30
tip: Go early — the bridge is quietest before 09:00, and the mountain is often clearest in the morning before the clouds roll in. Since 2026, tickets are valid for 3 consecutive days with unlimited cable-car rides.

name: Marble Mountains (Ngu Hanh Son)
address: 81 Huyen Tran Cong Chua Street, Ngu Hanh Son District, Da Nang (about 8 km south of the centre, on the road to Hoi An)
price: Thuy Son Mountain entry 40,000 VND (~$1.50) per adult; students 10,000 VND (~$0.40); under 6 free. Elevator 15,000 VND (~$0.60) one way, 30,000 VND (~$1.15) return. Am Phu Cave is a separate 20,000 VND (~$0.80).
hours: 07:00–17:30 daily (some sources say 17:00; ticket sales stop around 17:00)
tip: Climb to Huyen Khong Cave between 09:00 and 11:00, when sunlight pours through the cave opening. Bring cash — the gate is cash-only. Wear shoes with grip; the stone steps are steep and slippery when wet.

name: Linh Ung Pagoda, Son Tra
address: Hoang Sa Street, Tho Quang Ward, Son Tra Peninsula, Da Nang (about 10 km from the centre)
price: Free
tip: The 67-metre Lady Buddha statue is the tallest in Vietnam and looks out over the whole bay. Come at sunset for the best light, and dress modestly — shoulders and knees covered — since this is an active place of worship.

name: Son Tra Peninsula
address: Son Tra Peninsula, Da Nang
price: Free
tip: Ride the coastal road around the peninsula for the best sea views in the city, and keep an eye out for the rare red-shanked douc langurs in the trees near the top. Do not ride up after dark — the road is steep, unlit in places, and the monkeys cross it.

name: Dragon Bridge
address: Nguyen Van Linh Street, Hai Chau District, Da Nang (spans the Han River)
price: Free
hours: Open 24 hours; fire and water show on weekend evenings at 21:00 (Friday–Sunday according to most sources; some list Saturday–Sunday only — check locally)
tip: Watch from the riverside walkway on the east bank for the full view of the dragon. Arrive by 20:30 for a good spot, and expect crowds.

name: Museum of Cham Sculpture
address: 02 2 Thang 9 Street, Hai Chau District, Da Nang (near the Dragon Bridge)
price: 60,000 VND (~$2.30) per adult; students 10,000–20,000 VND (~$0.40–0.80); under 16 free
hours: 07:00–17:00 daily (some sources say 07:30–17:00; ticket desk closes around 16:30)
tip: The world's largest collection of Cham sculpture — sandstone gods and temple carvings from the ancient Champa kingdom, including many pieces recovered from My Son. Allow about an hour.

name: My Khe Beach
address: Vo Nguyen Giap Street, Son Tra District, Da Nang
price: Free
hours: Open 24 hours; lifeguards on duty during the day
tip: The best swimming is early morning or late afternoon, when the sun is off the sand. The beach is long, so walk south past the hotels for quieter stretches. The sea is roughest from October to December.

name: Han Market
address: 119 Tran Phu Street, Hai Chau District, Da Nang
price: Free to enter; bargain for souvenirs and fabric
tip: Come for the ground-floor food stalls (fresh fruit, dried seafood, local snacks) and the upstairs fabric and souvenir shops. Start bargaining at about half the first price and meet in the middle.

name: Con Market
address: 290 Hung Vuong Street, Hai Chau District, Da Nang
price: Free to enter
tip: Bigger and more local than Han Market — this is where Da Nang residents actually shop. The food court at the back is a great place for a cheap, honest lunch.

name: Mi Quang Ba Mua
address: 95 Nguyen Chi Thanh Street, Hai Chau District, Da Nang
price: About 40,000 VND (~$1.50) per bowl
tip: Order mi quang thit bo (beef) or mi quang tom thit (shrimp and pork). Add the rice crackers on the table — they are meant to be crumbled into the bowl.

name: Bun Cha Ca 109
address: 109 Nguyen Chi Thanh Street, Hai Chau District, Da Nang
price: About 35,000 VND (~$1.35) per bowl
tip: The fish cakes are made fresh in-house. Eat it the local way: squeeze in the lime, add chilli to taste, and eat it hot and fast.

name: Bun Cha Ca Ba Hoa
address: 27 Le Hong Phong Street, Hai Chau District, Da Nang
tip: A reliable breakfast spot, open all day. The broth is lighter and sweeter than the Hanoi version — very Central Vietnamese.

name: My Hanh Seafood
address: 03–05 Vo Nguyen Giap Street, Son Tra District, Da Nang
price: Not verified — seafood is priced by weight; agree the price before ordering
tip: Pick live seafood from the tanks and ask for the price per kilo first. Grilled scallops, garlic prawns and steamed clams with lemongrass are the safe bets.

name: Novotel Danang Premier Han River
address: 36 Bach Dang Street, Hai Chau District, Da Nang
price: Not verified — check on Agoda or Booking.com
tip: Mid-range to high-end, right on the river with views of the Dragon Bridge — book a river-view room if you want to watch the fire show from your window.

name: Furama Resort Danang
address: 103 Vo Nguyen Giap Street, Ngu Hanh Son District, Da Nang
price: Not verified — check on Agoda or Booking.com
tip: High-end beachfront resort on My Khe Beach, with a spa and direct beach access. Good for a splurge night or a family stay.

name: Hilton Da Nang
address: 50 Bach Dang Street, Hai Chau District, Da Nang
price: Not verified — check on Agoda or Booking.com
tip: High-end, on the river in the city centre — convenient for the markets, the Cham Museum and the Dragon Bridge.

name: Da Nang General Hospital
address: 124 Hai Phong Street, Hai Chau District, Da Nang
price: Not verified
tip: Phone: 0236 3821 118. This is the city's main public hospital. For international-standard care, ask your hotel to direct you to a private international clinic.

name: Non Nuoc Stone Carving Village
address: Huyen Tran Cong Chua Street, Hoa Hai Ward, Ngu Hanh Son District, Da Nang (at the foot of the Marble Mountains, about 8-9 km south of the city centre)
price: Not verified — small souvenirs are the affordable end; large statues are priced individually
tip: Small souvenir items are sometimes made from composite stone or resin rather than natural marble — ask the seller, and buy from a workshop where you can see carving in progress.

name: Jolie Cooking Class (Da Nang)
address: Meeting point 10 Tran Quoc Toan Street, Hai Chau District, Da Nang (near Da Nang Cathedral and Han Market); the home kitchen is at 14 An Trung Dong 6, Son Tra District — check your booking confirmation for which meeting point your package uses
price: About $40 per person for the market tour and cooking class (about 4.5 hours); about $66 per person for the full 6-hour farming, lantern and cooking experience
hours: Not verified — classes start about 08:30 or 14:30; check the booking page
tip: The market visit is a separate package from the cooking-only class — check what your booking includes before you go, and arrange your own transport to the meeting point.

name: Hoi An Ancient Town
address: Tran Phu Street, Hoi An Ancient Town, Da Nang
price: Walking the streets is free. Since 10 August 2026, entry to each heritage building costs 20,000 VND (~$0.80) per person, the same for Vietnamese and foreign visitors; children under 16 free. The old 120,000 VND ticket is no longer sold.
hours: Ticket booths 07:00–21:30 in summer, to 21:00 in winter; heritage sites about 08:30–17:30
tip: The 20,000 VND ticket covers one of 22 heritage sites — the assembly halls, old houses and museums. Buy tickets only at the official booths. On the full-moon lantern night each month, the electric lights go off around 18:00–22:00 and the town glows by lantern alone; remaining 2026 dates are 22 November and 22 December.

name: Japanese Covered Bridge (Chua Cau)
address: Nguyen Thi Minh Khai Street, Hoi An Ancient Town, Da Nang (at the Tran Phu end)
price: Entry via the heritage ticket, 20,000 VND (~$0.80) per site; children under 16 free
tip: The bridge is Hoi An's symbol — a 400-year-old covered bridge built by Japanese merchants, with a small temple inside. Come at dusk when the lanterns are lit, and look for the monkey and dog statues guarding each end.

name: My Son Sanctuary
address: Duy Phu Commune, Duy Xuyen District, Da Nang (about 35–40 km southwest of Hoi An, 45–60 minutes by car)
price: 150,000 VND (~$5.80) foreign adult; 100,000 VND (~$3.85) Vietnamese adult; children 5–15: 30,000 VND (~$1.15); under 5 free. Includes the electric shuttle, museum and Cham dance shows at 09:30 and 10:30.
hours: 06:00–18:00 daily, last tickets 17:00 (some sources list closing at 17:00)
tip: Go before 08:15 or after 15:30 to avoid the tour-bus crowds and the midday heat. The brick Hindu temples of the Champa kingdom, built between the 4th and 13th centuries, sit in a jungle valley — allow at least 2 hours.

name: Bay Mau Coconut Forest (Cam Thanh)
address: DX18 Road, Cam Thanh Commune, Hoi An, Da Nang (about 5 km east of the Old Town)
price: Entry about 30,000 VND (~$1.15) per person; basket boat about 150,000–200,000 VND (~$6–8) per boat for two people, 45–60 minutes. Prices vary by operator — confirm before boarding. A tip of 20,000–50,000 VND (~$0.80–1.90) for the rower is customary.
tip: The round basket boats (thung chai) spin, the rowers sing, and you will get splashed — wear clothes you do not mind getting wet. Book through your hotel or a reputable operator rather than the touts at the car park.

name: An Bang Beach
address: Nguyen Phan Vinh Street, Cam An Ward, Hoi An, Da Nang (about 4 km from the Old Town)
price: Free
tip: Hoi An's best beach — long, sandy and much quieter than the town. Come for sunset, when the fishing boats come in and the beach bars light up. The sea is calmest from February to August.

name: Tra Que Vegetable Village
address: Hai Ba Trung Road, Cam Ha Commune, Hoi An, Da Nang (about 2.5 km from the Ancient Town)
price: Not verified — cooking classes and farming experiences are sold by local operators; agree the price before booking
tip: A 400-year-old farming village that grows the herbs for Hoi An's kitchens. The hands-on experiences — planting, watering, and cooking with a local family — are the highlight, and a great morning out with kids.

name: Hoi An Night Market
address: Nguyen Hoang Street, An Hoi, Hoi An, Da Nang
price: Free to enter
hours: Evening, from about 17:00 — exact hours not verified
tip: Hundreds of lantern stalls across the river from the Old Town. Lanterns make a lovely souvenir and pack flat — bargain politely, and check the wiring before you buy an electric one.

name: Hoai River Lantern Boat Ride
address: Bach Dang Street riverfront, Hoi An Ancient Town, Da Nang
price: About 170,000 VND (~$6.50) for up to 3 people
hours: Evening, from about 17:00 — exact hours not verified
tip: The classic Hoi An photo: a wooden boat, a paper lantern, and the old town glowing behind you. Agree the price and the length of the ride before you step on board, and buy your floating lantern from the boat vendor, not from touts on the street.

name: Banh Mi Phuong
address: 2B Phan Chau Trinh Street, Hoi An, Da Nang
tip: The banh mi shop Anthony Bourdain made famous. Expect a queue at lunch — it moves fast. Order the classic mixed (thap cam) and eat it standing on the street like everyone else.

name: Madam Khanh — The Banh Mi Queen
address: 115 Tran Cao Van Street, Hoi An, Da Nang
tip: The locals' favourite, and the one most Hoi An residents will send you to first. The egg and pork version is excellent, and the queue is usually shorter than at Phuong.

name: Morning Glory Restaurant
address: 106 Nguyen Thai Hoc Street, Hoi An, Da Nang
tip: The best place to try cao lau and white rose dumplings in one sitting, in a beautiful old house. It is the most tourist-oriented restaurant on this list — and the food earns it.

name: Cao Lau Thanh
address: 26 Thai Phien Street, Hoi An, Da Nang
price: Not verified
tip: A small, local spot for cao lau away from the main tourist streets. Order cao lau and a fresh beer, and sit with the regulars.

name: White Rose Restaurant
address: 533 Hai Ba Trung Street, Hoi An, Da Nang
price: Not verified
tip: White rose dumplings — delicate shrimp dumplings shaped like roses — are a Hoi An invention, and this family-run restaurant is where they started.

name: Com Ga Ba Nga
address: 8 Phan Chau Trinh Street, Hoi An, Da Nang
price: Not verified
tip: Chicken rice the Hoi An way: shredded chicken, turmeric rice, pickled onions and herbs. A proper lunch for very little money.

name: Anantara Hoi An Resort
address: 1 Pham Hong Thai Street, Hoi An, Da Nang
price: Not verified — check on Agoda or Booking.com
tip: High-end riverside resort on the edge of the Old Town — colonial-style rooms, a pool on the river, and a short walk to the lanterns.

name: La Siesta Hoi An Resort & Spa
address: 132–134 Hung Vuong Street, Hoi An, Da Nang
price: Not verified — check on Agoda or Booking.com
tip: High-end, a 10-minute walk from the Old Town, with a spa and a rooftop pool. Good for couples who want quiet after the lanterns.

name: Little Riverside Hoi An
address: 9 Phan Boi Chau Street, Hoi An, Da Nang
price: Not verified — check on Agoda or Booking.com
tip: Mid-range boutique hotel on the river, a few minutes' walk from the Old Town — good value for the location.

name: Little Hoi An Boutique Hotel & Spa
address: 2 Thoai Ngoc Hau Street, Hoi An, Da Nang
price: Not verified — check on Agoda or Booking.com
tip: Mid-range, in the old town area with a spa and pool. Ask for a room away from the street if you are a light sleeper.

name: Da Nang General Hospital
address: 124 Hai Phong Street, Hai Chau District, Da Nang (about 30 km from Hoi An — the nearest major hospital)
price: Not verified
tip: Phone: 0236 3821 118. Hoi An has small local clinics for minor issues, but anything serious goes to Da Nang. Keep your travel insurance details on your phone.

name: Hoi An Silk Village
address: 28 Nguyen Tat Thanh Street, Hoi An
price: Not verified — silk fabric about $10-25 (about 260,000-650,000 VND) per metre in the Central Market area; ask in the shop
hours: Not verified — check on Google Maps
tip: Real silk feels cool, smooth and slightly uneven, and wrinkles when you scrunch it. If you want a suit or dress made, allow at least 24 hours and one fitting.

name: Banh Dau Xanh Ba Trinh
address: 62 Le Loi Street, Hoi An
price: About 25,000 VND (~$1) per box (one source; other Hoi An mung bean cakes run about 25,000-50,000 VND per box)
hours: Not verified — check on Google Maps
tip: Buy it with a box of the meat-filled version if you eat meat — it is the one locals recommend for gifts. Eat it with hot tea, the way it is meant to be eaten.

name: Thanh Ha Pottery Village
address: Pham Phan Street, Thanh Ha, Hoi An (about 3 km west of the Ancient Town)
price: Entrance ticket about 35,000 VND (~$1) per adult, 15,000 VND (~$0.60) per child (some sources list 30,000 VND — see Unverified); pottery-making about 30,000-40,000 VND (~$1-2) per person at the museum workshop; small souvenirs from about 20,000 VND (~$1)
tip: The ticket includes a small gift (usually a clay animal whistle) and a voucher for the museum shop. If a workshop asks you to buy a 200,000-800,000 VND piece to take part, walk to the next one — the standard making fee is small.

name: Lantern-Making Workshop (April Adventure Travel)
address: Alley of 05 Tran Phu Street (05/2 Tran Phu, opposite Pho Hoi Hotel), Hoi An Ancient Town
price: About $8-9 per person for the 1-hour workshop (about 200,000-235,000 VND), lantern included; about $17-18 for the workshop plus boat ride version
hours: Not verified — daytime and evening sessions; check availability when booking
tip: Go for a late-afternoon session so you finish as the town's lanterns light up — then carry your own lantern down to the river.

name: Tra Que Vegetable Village
address: Tra Que Village, Cam Ha, Hoi An (about 3 km north of the Ancient Town); tours commonly meet at 119 Tran Quang Khai Street or 12 Cua Dai Street, Hoi An
price: From about $25 per person for a cycling and farming tour (about 3.5 hours) to about $35 per person for the full farming and cooking class (about 5 hours, with meal included); prices vary by operator
hours: Tours usually start about 08:30-08:45; the village itself is a working farming village
tip: Wear shoes you can get muddy and bring sun protection — you will be in the fields, not watching from a path. Tell the operator in advance if you are vegetarian; the cooking class adapts easily.

name: Cam Ranh International Airport
address: Cam Ranh International Airport, Cam Ranh City, Khanh Hoa Province
price: Airport shuttle bus 50,000–65,000 VND (~$2–$2.50); taxi to central Nha Trang 300,000–400,000 VND (~$12–$15)
hours: Open 24 hours; shuttle bus runs roughly 05:30–23:00
tip: Ignore the drivers who approach you in the arrivals hall. The official taxi stand is outside, and the shuttle bus stop is clearly signed. If your hotel offers a pickup, take it — it is usually the same price as a taxi with none of the hassle.

name: Nha Trang Railway Station
address: 17 Thai Nguyen Street, Nha Trang, Khanh Hoa Province
price: Train to Ho Chi Minh City from ~347,000 VND (~$13) for a seat; 4-berth sleeper from ~591,000 VND (~$23)
hours: Ticket counters open daily; 7 trains a day to Ho Chi Minh City
tip: The station is a 10-minute Grab ride from Tran Phu beach. The overnight SNT1 sleeper (20:20 departure from Nha Trang) is the most popular way back to Saigon.

name: VinWonders Nha Trang
address: Hon Tre Island, Nha Trang, Khanh Hoa Province
price: Standard adult ticket 1,050,000 VND (~$40) including round-trip cable car; children 100–140 cm and seniors 60+ 800,000 VND (~$31); after 16:00 adult ticket 700,000 VND (~$27); children under 100 cm free
hours: Park 8:30–20:00 daily; cable car runs until about 22:00 (last return often 21:30–22:00)
tip: The sea-crossing cable car is an attraction in itself — 8 minutes over the bay with the whole coastline below you. Arrive at opening to beat the heat and the queues, and save the water park for the afternoon. Note that the cable car sometimes closes for maintenance (it was closed 26 October–10 November 2026, with speedboats replacing it) — check before you go.

name: Po Nagar Cham Towers
address: 61 Hai Thang Tu Street, Nha Trang, Khanh Hoa Province
price: 30,000 VND (~$1.15) per person
tip: These red-brick Cham towers, built between the 7th and 13th centuries, sit on a hill above the Cai River about 2 km north of the center. Come early for soft light on the brickwork and fewer tour groups, and watch for the Cham dance performances, which usually run mid-morning. It is still an active place of worship — dress modestly and keep quiet inside the towers.

name: Long Son Pagoda
address: 22 Duong 23 Thang 10 Street, Nha Trang, Khanh Hoa Province
price: Free entry; donations welcome
tip: Climb the 150-plus steps to the giant white Buddha on the hilltop for the best panorama in the city — go late in the afternoon when the light turns golden and the heat eases. Cover your shoulders and knees, and remove your shoes before entering the main hall.

name: Nha Trang Beach (Tran Phu Beach)
address: Tran Phu Street, Nha Trang, Khanh Hoa Province
price: Free; sun loungers and umbrellas from beach vendors cost extra
hours: Open all day; lifeguards on duty during daylight hours
tip: The sand is cleanest and the water calmest in the morning. The southern end near the Novotel is quieter; the stretch in front of the central hotels is where the action is. Swim inside the marked areas — the currents can be strong after rain.

name: Hon Chong Promontory
address: Pham Van Dong Street, Nha Trang, Khanh Hoa Province
price: Not verified — check at the ticket counter
tip: A cluster of huge granite boulders at the northern end of the bay, famous as the backdrop for the film *The Lover*. Sunset here, with the fishing boats and the city lights, is one of Nha Trang's best free shows. The small cafe on the rocks is a good place to sit it out.

name: Nha Trang Cathedral (Christ the King Cathedral)
address: 31 Thai Nguyen Street, Nha Trang, Khanh Hoa Province
price: Free admission
hours: Not verified — check at the gate
tip: A French-built stone church on a hill above the railway station, with a lovely quiet courtyard. It photographs best in the morning, when the stone glows warm in the sun.

name: National Oceanographic Museum
address: 1 Cau Da Street, Nha Trang, Khanh Hoa Province
price: Not verified — check at the ticket counter (museums in the city typically charge up to 40,000 VND)
hours: Not verified — check before you go
tip: A charming old-school museum at Cau Da Port with aquariums, whale skeletons, and deep-sea specimens. A good rainy-day stop, and it pairs well with a boat trip from the same pier.

name: Dam Market
address: Ben Cho Street, Nha Trang, Khanh Hoa Province
price: Free to enter
tip: The city's main market for over 100 years — dried squid, fish sauce, coffee, and souvenirs under one roof, plus food stalls serving jellyfish noodles and fish-cake soup from early morning. Bargain politely and come hungry. It is about 2 km from the beachfront, an easy Grab ride.

name: I-Resort Nha Trang (mud bath and hot springs)
address: Xuan Ngoc area, Nha Trang, Khanh Hoa Province
price: Mud bath packages from around 350,000 VND (~$13) per person; prices vary by package — check at the counter
tip: The most complete mud-bath experience on the mainland: mineral mud pools, hot springs, waterfalls, and gardens. Go in the afternoon after sightseeing, and bring a swimsuit. If I-Resort is busy, Thap Ba Hot Spring (438 Ngo Den Street) is the older, simpler alternative — mineral pool from 120,000 VND (~$4.60), mud bath 260,000–350,000 VND (~$10–$13) per person.

name: Ba Ho Waterfalls
address: Van Thuan Village, Ninh Ich Commune, Ninh Hoa Town, Khanh Hoa Province (about 25 km north of Nha Trang)
price: 100,000 VND (~$4) per person
hours: Not verified — daytime only; go in the morning
tip: Three tiers of waterfalls and natural pools in the jungle, reached by a rocky climb — wear proper shoes, not flip-flops, and bring water. The pools are swimmable in the dry season. Cliff-jumping is popular but the rocks are unforgiving; jump only where locals do, and never alone.

name: Hon Mun Island (snorkeling day trip)
address: Hon Mun Island, Nha Trang Bay, Khanh Hoa Province (boats leave from Cau Da Port)
price: Day trips typically 400,000–800,000 VND (~$15–$31) per person including boat, snorkeling gear, and lunch — book through your hotel or a licensed operator
hours: Boats leave in the morning, usually 8:00–9:00, and return mid-afternoon
tip: Hon Mun is a marine protected area with the best coral and fish diversity in the bay. Go February to August for calm water and good visibility. Do not touch or stand on the coral, and wear reef-safe sunscreen.

name: Nem Nuong Dang Van Quyen
address: 16A Lan Ong Street, Nha Trang, Khanh Hoa Province (second branch at 2–4 Phan Boi Chau Street)
price: Around 50,000–100,000 VND (~$2–$4) per person
tip: The most famous nem nuong in town, a 3-minute walk from Dam Market. The set comes with grilled pork skewers, rice paper, herbs, green mango, and a rich peanut dipping sauce. It is a hands-on meal — wrap it yourself, and do not be shy about the herbs.

name: Lac Canh Grilled Beef Restaurant
address: 77 Nguyen Binh Khiem Street, Nha Trang, Khanh Hoa Province
price: Around 150,000–250,000 VND (~$6–$10) per person
tip: A Nha Trang institution for decades. Small pieces of marinated beef are grilled at your table on a charcoal stove, then eaten with fresh vegetables and dipping sauce. It gets smoky and busy in the evening — that is part of the fun. Come early to get a table.

name: Dam Market food stalls
address: Ben Cho Street, Nha Trang, Khanh Hoa Province
hours: 5:00–18:30 daily; food stalls busiest in the morning
tip: The cheapest and most local breakfast in town: bun cha ca, bun sua, and banh can (small savory rice pancakes) from the stalls inside the market. Point, smile, and sit on the small plastic stools like everyone else.

name: InterContinental Nha Trang
address: 32–34 Tran Phu Street, Nha Trang, Khanh Hoa Province
price: Room rates vary by season — Not verified, check on Agoda or Booking.com
tip: The most polished beachfront address in the city, with a rooftop pool and a superb breakfast. Right on the promenade, a 5-minute walk from the night market.

name: Sheraton Nha Trang Hotel & Spa
address: 26–28 Tran Phu Street, Nha Trang, Khanh Hoa Province
price: Room rates vary by season — Not verified, check on Agoda or Booking.com
tip: A reliable 5-star on the beachfront with a big pool, a good spa, and sea-view rooms that are worth the upgrade. A solid choice for families.

name: Galina Hotel & Spa
address: 31 Hung Vuong Street, Nha Trang, Khanh Hoa Province
price: Room rates vary by season — Not verified, check on Agoda or Booking.com
tip: A well-priced 4-star one block back from the beach, with a rooftop pool and a mud-bath spa on site. Good value for the location.

name: Vinpearl Resort Nha Trang
address: Hon Tre Island, Nha Trang, Khanh Hoa Province
price: Room rates vary by season — Not verified, check on Agoda or Booking.com
tip: Stay on the island itself if you want the resort experience: private beach, cable car access, and VinWonders next door. Best for families planning two days on Hon Tre.

name: Khanh Hoa General Hospital
address: 19 Yersin Street, Nha Trang, Khanh Hoa Province
price: Emergency care fees vary — Not verified
tip: The city's main public hospital. For minor issues, the international clinics on Tran Phu are faster and English-speaking — ask your hotel for the nearest one. Travel insurance is strongly recommended.

name: Sanest Bird's Nest Showroom
address: 89 Thong Nhat Street, Nha Trang, Khanh Hoa Province
price: From about 3,000,000 VND (~$115) per 100 g of dried nest; ready-to-drink bottles cost much less
tip: The official showroom of the Khanh Hoa Salanganes Nest Company — the safest place in town to buy real bird's nest. Ask staff to explain the grades before you pay.

name: Dam Market (Cho Dam)
address: Ben Cho Street, Van Thanh Ward, Nha Trang, Khanh Hoa Province
price: Dried squid about 500,000–700,000 VND (~$19–27) per kg; other dried goods and nem chua priced at the stall
hours: Not verified — sources list 4:00 AM–6:30 PM and 5:00 AM–6:30 PM
tip: The city's central market and the best one-stop shop for dried seafood, nem chua and mango rice paper. Bargain politely on gift items — aim for 10–20% off the first price. Food stalls are fixed-price.

name: Lien Khuong International Airport (DLI)
address: Lien Khuong Airport, Duc Trong District, Lam Dong Province, about 30 km south of Da Lat city centre
price: Taxi to the city centre roughly 250,000–350,000 VND (~$10–13)
tip: The airport fully reopened after runway works in August 2026. Pre-book your transfer or use the official taxi counter — do not accept offers from drivers inside the terminal.

name: Da Lat Railway Station
address: 1 Quang Trung Street, Da Lat City, Lam Dong Province
price: Entry about 50,000 VND (~$2); waived if you ride the train
tip: No regular long-distance trains run from here anymore — come for the 1930s Art Deco building (its three peaked roofs echo Langbiang's peaks) and the short heritage ride to Trai Mat village, about 7 km away.

name: Crazy House (Hang Nga Guesthouse)
address: 3 Huynh Thuc Khang Street, Da Lat City, Lam Dong Province
price: Adult 80,000 VND (~$3), child 30,000 VND (~$1)
hours: Not verified — daytime; check on Google Maps before you go
tip: A surreal, tree-shaped house designed by architect Dang Viet Nga — winding staircases, cave-like rooms, animal-themed spaces and narrow bridges with no railings. Go early in the morning to have it nearly to yourself, and hold small children's hands on the stairs. Allow 1–1.5 hours.

name: Datanla Waterfall
address: Datanla Waterfall, Prenn Pass, National Highway 20, about 5 km south of Da Lat city centre, Lam Dong Province
price: Entrance about 50,000 VND (~$2); the new 2.4 km alpine coaster about 250,000 VND (~$10) round trip
hours: Not verified — daytime; check on Google Maps before you go
tip: The waterfall itself is a 20 m cascade in the forest; the alpine coaster is the real draw — you control your own speed as you glide down through the pines. Go on a weekday morning to avoid queues. Allow 1.5–2 hours.

name: Langbiang Mountain
address: Langbiang Mountain, about 12 km north of Da Lat city centre, Lac Duong District, Lam Dong Province
price: Entrance adult 50,000 VND (~$2), child under 1.2 m 25,000 VND (~$1). Shared jeep to Radar Peak about 120,000 VND (~$5) per person; a private jeep for up to 6 people about 720,000 VND (~$28).
hours: About 7:00–21:00 daily (not verified — check on arrival)
tip: Da Lat's highest mountain at 2,167 m, with views over the city, Golden and Silver streams, and Suoi Vang Lake. Hike the road to the 1,929 m Radar Peak in about 2 hours, or take the jeep (15–20 minutes) and save your knees. Best November to March, when the skies are clearest. Bring a jacket — it is windy at the top.

name: Xuan Huong Lake
address: Xuan Huong Lake, city centre, Da Lat City, Lam Dong Province
price: Free to walk around; swan pedal boats roughly 60,000–100,000 VND (~$2–4) per boat (not verified — check at the lake)
tip: The heart of the city. Walk the 5 km loop at sunrise, when mist sits on the water and the city is quiet, or come at sunset for the lights. The Lam Vien Square flower dome at the lake's edge is the city's most photographed landmark.

name: Truc Lam Zen Monastery & Tuyen Lam Lake
address: Truc Lam Zen Monastery, Tuyen Lam Lake, about 6 km south of Da Lat city centre, Lam Dong Province
price: Free entry to the monastery; cable car from Robin Hill about 100,000–150,000 VND (~$4–6) one way (not verified — check at the counter)
tip: A peaceful working monastery in pine forest above a still lake — the quietest, most beautiful place in Da Lat. Dress modestly (cover shoulders and knees), speak softly, and do not photograph monks without asking. The cable car from Robin Hill gives you a lovely ride over the forest. Allow half a day with the lake.

name: Clay Tunnel (Duong Ham Dat Set)
address: Tuyen Lam Lake area, about 13 km south of Da Lat city centre, Lam Dong Province
price: About 120,000 VND (~$5) per person (not verified — check at the counter)
tip: A long outdoor sculpture tunnel telling Da Lat's history in red clay — part art, part photo playground, with lake views at the end. Best combined with Truc Lam Monastery and Tuyen Lam Lake in one half-day.

name: Bao Dai Summer Palace
address: 1 Trieu Viet Vuong Street, Da Lat City, Lam Dong Province
price: Not verified — check at the ticket counter
tip: The Art Deco summer home of Vietnam's last emperor, kept much as it was in the 1930s–40s. A gentle, interesting hour for history lovers, with gardens and pine trees around it.

name: Lien Hoa Bakery & Restaurant
address: Not verified — please check on Google Maps
price: Mains roughly 50,000–150,000 VND (~$2–6)
tip: A Da Lat institution for banh can, noodles and baked goods. Come for breakfast before the tour buses arrive.

name: Da Lat Night Market
address: Nguyen Thi Minh Khai Street, city centre, Da Lat City, Lam Dong Province
price: Street snacks 20,000–60,000 VND (~$1–2); hot soy milk about 15,000–20,000 VND (~$1)
tip: The evening ritual: grilled rice paper, roast sweet potatoes, hot soy milk and strawberries. Go hungry, bring small notes, and dress warmly — it gets cold after dark.

name: The Married Beans Coffee (or any lakeside cafe)
address: Not verified — please check on Google Maps
price: Coffee roughly 40,000–80,000 VND (~$2–3)
tip: Da Lat runs on coffee. The Central Highlands grow Vietnam's best arabica, and the lakeside cafes are made for slow mornings. Order ca phe sua da (iced coffee with condensed milk) or try a pour-over of local arabica.

name: Ana Mandara Villas Dalat Resort & Spa
address: Not verified — please check on Google Maps
price: High-end; roughly 2,500,000–5,000,000 VND (~$96–192) per night (check at booking)
tip: Restored 1920s–30s French villas in pine gardens on a hill above town. The most romantic stay in Da Lat — book a villa with a fireplace for the cold months.

name: Dalat Palace Heritage Hotel
address: 12 Tran Phu Street, Da Lat City, Lam Dong Province
price: High-end; roughly 3,000,000–6,000,000 VND (~$115–231) per night (check at booking)
tip: The grand old hotel facing the lake, built in 1922. Best for a splurge and for its location — step out and you are on the lake promenade.

name: The Common Room Project (hostel)
address: Not verified — please check on Google Maps
price: Budget; dorm beds roughly 150,000–250,000 VND (~$6–10), private rooms roughly 400,000–700,000 VND (~$15–27) (check at booking)
tip: A friendly, well-run hostel in the centre with good local advice and motorbike rental. Book ahead for December–January weekends.

name: Lam Dong General Hospital
address: 4 Pham Ngoc Thach Street, Da Lat City, Lam Dong Province
price: Not verified
tip: The main public hospital in the city. For international-standard care, the nearest options are in Ho Chi Minh City, about 6–8 hours by road. Carry travel insurance.

name: L'angfarm Store
address: 6 Nguyen Thi Minh Khai, Ward 1, Da Lat, Lam Dong Province
price: Not verified — check in store; packaged coffee, tea, jam and dried fruit are mid-range gift prices
tip: The Da Lat-born specialty chain — the easiest one-stop gift shop in town, with clean packaging and fixed prices (no bargaining needed). Several branches around the centre; this one is the most central.

name: Da Lat Night Market
address: Gate at 4 Nguyen Thi Minh Khai Street, Ward 1, Da Lat, Lam Dong Province
price: Not verified — check at the stall; jam, dried fruit, tea and coffee are sold by weight or by the bag
hours: Not verified — sources list 5:00 PM–10:00 PM and 5:00 AM–10:00 PM
tip: The night stalls are the place to taste everything — dried fruit, jam, artichoke tea — before you buy. Start bargaining at about half the quoted price on souvenirs; food is fixed-price. Bring cash and a warm layer.

name: Van Thanh Flower Village
address: 40 Van Thanh Street, Ward 5, Da Lat, Lam Dong Province
price: Not verified — sources list 40,000–100,000 VND (~$2–4) per adult, and some farms are free
tip: Best in the dry season, November to March, when the blooms are at their most vivid. Allow 1–2 hours, and combine it with a coffee farm stop on the same road out of town.

name: Biofresh Strawberry Farm
address: Than Tho Lake area, Ho Xuan Huong Street, Ward 10, Da Lat, Lam Dong Province
price: Entry about 10,000–20,000 VND (~$0.40–0.80); strawberries roughly 200,000–400,000 VND (~$8–15) per kg in season — check at the farm
tip: Best November to April. Bring a hat and sunscreen — the greenhouses are warm — and a small bag for your berries.

name: Me Linh Coffee Garden
address: Group 20, Hamlet 4, Ta Nung, Da Lat, Lam Dong Province
price: Not verified — check at the garden; coffee tasting prices not verified
tip: Go for the view and the plantation walk as much as the coffee. The weasel coffee is strong and expensive — share one cup between two if you are only curious.

name: Tan Son Nhat International Airport
address: Truong Son Street, Tan Binh Ward, Ho Chi Minh City
price: Grab to District 1 roughly 110,000–250,000 VND (~$4–$10)
tip: Use the Grab pickup point shown in the app, and ignore drivers who approach you inside the terminal offering a "cheap" fixed price.

name: Saigon Railway Station
address: 1 Nguyen Thong Street, Ho Chi Minh City
price: Train to Nha Trang from ~347,000 VND (~$13) for a seat; sleeper berths from ~591,000 VND (~$23)
hours: Ticket counters open daily; trains run day and night — check the timetable before you go
tip: Book sleeper berths a few days ahead in high season; lower berths cost more but are easier to climb into.

name: War Remnants Museum
address: 28 Vo Van Tan Street, Ho Chi Minh City
price: 60,000 VND (~$2.30) per adult since 1 October 2026; reduced admission 30,000 VND (~$1.15); children under 6 free
hours: 7:30–17:30 daily, including public holidays; ticket counter closes at 17:00
tip: The outdoor display of tanks and aircraft is free to look at from the courtyard, but the indoor photo exhibitions are the heart of the visit — and they are graphic. Allow 1.5 to 2 hours, and plan something light afterwards.

name: Independence Palace (Reunification Palace)
address: 135 Nam Ky Khoi Nghia Street, Ho Chi Minh City
price: Full ticket (palace + exhibition) 80,000 VND (~$3) per adult; palace-only ticket 40,000 VND (~$1.50); students and seniors 40,000 VND; children 20,000 VND
hours: 7:00–18:00 daily, including public holidays and Tet
tip: Go at opening time for empty rooms and soft light in the reception halls. The basement command bunker and the two tanks on the front lawn are the highlights — the tanks are replicas of the ones that crashed the gates on 30 April 1975.

name: Ben Thanh Market
address: Le Loi Street, Ho Chi Minh City
price: Free to enter; expect to bargain hard — vendors often start at 2 to 3 times the real price
hours: Day market about 6:00–18:00 daily; night market around the building about 18:00–22:00
tip: Come before 9:00 AM for cooler air and more flexible prices. The food stalls at the back serve excellent pho and broken rice — eat where the locals are sitting.

name: Saigon Central Post Office
address: 2 Cong Xa Paris Street, Ho Chi Minh City
price: Free to enter
hours: Not verified — check at the door
tip: Step inside for the vaulted hall, the giant portrait of Ho Chi Minh, and the old phone booths. It is still a working post office, so you can actually mail a postcard home.

name: Notre-Dame Cathedral Basilica of Saigon
address: 1 Cong Xa Paris Street, Ho Chi Minh City
price: Free to view from outside
hours: Not verified — the cathedral has been closed for restoration, so plan on viewing the exterior only
tip: The twin red-brick towers photograph best in the late afternoon, with the Post Office across the square in the same frame.

name: Saigon Opera House
address: 7 Lam Son Square, Ho Chi Minh City
price: Show tickets vary by performance — Not verified, check at the box office
hours: Open for performances, usually in the evening
tip: The AO Show (a mix of acrobatics, dance, and bamboo circus) is the most visitor-friendly performance. Book a few days ahead.

name: Bitexco Financial Tower — Saigon Skydeck
address: 2 Hai Trieu Street, Ho Chi Minh City
price: 240,000 VND (~$9) per adult
tip: Come at sunset for the city lights coming on along the Saigon River. The 49th-floor Skydeck is the classic viewpoint; Landmark 81 across the river now has a taller deck if you want the highest view in Vietnam.

name: Cu Chi Tunnels (Ben Dinh site)
address: Ben Dinh Hamlet, Nhuan Duc Commune, Cu Chi District, Ho Chi Minh City
price: 135,000 VND (~$5.20) per foreign visitor (35,000 VND site fee + 100,000 VND guiding/service ticket, since 1 February 2026); children under 6 free
tip: Ben Dinh is the closer, busier site (about 50 km, 1.5 hours from the center); Ben Duoc, about 70 km out, is quieter and more spread out. Most half-day tours go to Ben Dinh and include transport — budget around 500,000–700,000 VND (~$19–$27) per person for a group tour with pickup. Wear shoes you can get muddy and clothes you do not mind crawling in; the tunnel sections are short but tight and hot.

name: Jade Emperor Pagoda
address: 73 Mai Thi Luu Street, Ho Chi Minh City
price: Free entry; donations welcome
hours: Not verified — check at the gate
tip: Go early in the morning when the incense smoke is thick and the chanting starts. It is one of the city's most atmospheric temples, and far less crowded than the central sights.

name: Binh Tay Market (Cholon)
address: 57A Thap Muoi Street, Ho Chi Minh City
price: Free to enter
hours: Not verified — daytime market, busiest in the morning
tip: This is Cholon's wholesale heart — far more local than Ben Thanh, and the place to see how the city really shops. Pair it with Thien Hau Temple, a 10-minute walk away.

name: Thien Hau Temple
address: 710 Nguyen Trai Street, Ho Chi Minh City
price: Free entry
hours: Not verified — check at the gate
tip: Look up: hundreds of incense coils hang from the ceiling, and the rooftop ceramic figures are some of the finest in the city. It is an active temple, so dress modestly and keep your voice down.

name: Bui Vien Walking Street
address: Bui Vien Street, Ho Chi Minh City
price: Free to walk; bars and food stalls set their own prices
hours: Pedestrian-only in the evenings; liveliest after 19:00
tip: Fun for one evening of people-watching and cheap beer, but keep your bag in front of you and agree on drink prices before you sit down — a few bars here have a reputation for surprise bills.

name: Pho Hoa Pasteur
address: 260C Pasteur Street, Ho Chi Minh City
price: Around 60,000–80,000 VND (~$2.30–$3) per bowl
tip: In business since 1968 and holding a Michelin Bib Gourmand. Order the pho dac biet (special) and add the fresh herbs and bean sprouts from the table basket. It is a 10-minute Grab ride from Ben Thanh.

name: Banh Mi Huynh Hoa
address: 26 Le Thi Rieng Street, Ho Chi Minh City
price: Around 30,000–40,000 VND (~$1.15–$1.50) per sandwich
tip: The most famous banh mi in the city — pate, cold cuts, pork floss, and pickled vegetables, packed until the baguette nearly bursts. The line moves fast. Eat it on the spot; it does not travel well.

name: Com Tam Ba Ghien
address: 84 Dang Van Ngu Street, Ho Chi Minh City
price: Around 60,000–80,000 VND (~$2.30–$3) per plate
hours: Not verified — check at the door
tip: A Saigon institution for nearly 30 years. The grilled pork chop is the star — thick, smoky, and bigger than the plate. It is in Phu Nhuan, a short Grab ride north of the center.

name: Cuc Gach Quan
address: 10 Dang Tat Street, Ho Chi Minh City
price: Not verified — mid-range by Saigon standards, roughly 150,000–300,000 VND (~$6–$12) per person
hours: Not verified — check at the door
tip: The prettiest Vietnamese restaurant in the city — a converted French-era house full of antiques, serving home-style dishes like caramelized pork in clay pot and morning glory with garlic. Book ahead for dinner.

name: Hum Vegetarian
address: 32 Vo Van Tan Street, Ho Chi Minh City
price: Not verified — mid-range, roughly 150,000–250,000 VND (~$6–$10) per person
hours: Not verified — check at the door
tip: The city's best-known vegetarian restaurant, set in a calm garden villa near the War Remnants Museum. The menu is entirely plant-based and the lotus rice is the signature. Good for a quiet lunch after the museum.

name: Hotel Continental Saigon
address: 132–134 Dong Khoi Street, Ho Chi Minh City
price: Room rates vary by season — Not verified, check on Agoda or Booking.com
tip: A colonial-era classic facing the Opera House, in business since 1880. Mid-range prices for a grand old address, and the ground-floor terrace is a lovely spot for a slow breakfast.

name: Park Hyatt Saigon
address: 2 Lam Son Square, Ho Chi Minh City
price: Room rates vary by season — Not verified, check on Agoda or Booking.com
tip: The city's most refined hotel, on Lam Son Square beside the Opera House. The pool and spa are a genuine oasis after a day in the heat.

name: The Reverie Saigon
address: 22–36 Nguyen Hue Boulevard, Ho Chi Minh City
price: Room rates vary by season — Not verified, check on Agoda or Booking.com
tip: The most over-the-top luxury in the city, in the Times Square building on Nguyen Hue Walking Street. The Italian-designed suites are extraordinary, and the rooftop bar has one of the best skyline views in Saigon.

name: Cho Ray Hospital
address: 201B Nguyen Chi Thanh Street, Ho Chi Minh City
price: Emergency care fees vary — Not verified
tip: The city's largest public hospital. For minor issues, the international clinics in District 1 and District 7 are faster and English-speaking — ask your hotel for the nearest one. Travel insurance is strongly recommended.

name: Hoa's Kitchen — Vietnamese Homestyle Cooking Class
address: Meeting point 670/81 Doan Van Bo Street, Ward 8, District 4, Ho Chi Minh City
price: From about £36 per person (about $48) on GetYourGuide — check the current price before booking
hours: About 3 hours; start times vary — check availability when booking
tip: Book on GetYourGuide (search "Vietnamese Homestyle Cooking Class", provider Hoa's Kitchen) — free cancellation up to 24 hours in advance, reserve now and pay later. Tell Hoa in advance about allergies or dietary needs; there are no separate cooking stations, everyone cooks the same menu together.

name: Can Tho International Airport (VCA)
address: 179B Le Hong Phong Street, Tra Noc Ward, Binh Thuy District, Can Tho City
price: Taxi to the city centre 150,000–250,000 VND (~$6–10)
tip: The taxi counter inside the terminal is the safest bet; Grab pickup is outside. The ride takes 15–25 minutes.

name: Mien Tay Bus Station (Ho Chi Minh City departure point)
address: 395 Kinh Duong Vuong Street, An Lac Ward, Binh Tan District, Ho Chi Minh City
price: Bus to Can Tho about 95,000–180,000 VND (~$4–7)
tip: Buy tickets at the official counters inside the station, not from touts outside. Allow an extra hour to get to the station from central Ho Chi Minh City in traffic.

name: Ninh Kieu Wharf (boat departure point)
address: Hai Ba Trung Street, Ninh Kieu District, Can Tho City
price: Boat hire to Cai Rang — see section D
tip: This is where most floating market boats depart. Come the evening before to look at the boats and agree a price, so your 5 a.m. start is painless.

name: Cai Rang Floating Market
address: Cai Rang Floating Market, Can Tho River, about 6 km south-west of Can Tho city centre, Can Tho City
price: No entry fee. Private sampan (2–4 people) about 200,000–350,000 VND (~$8–13) per boat; private motorboat (up to 8 people) about 400,000–600,000 VND (~$15–23); group tour boat about 80,000–150,000 VND (~$3–6) per person. Hotel tours with guide and breakfast about 250,000–500,000 VND (~$10–19) per person. Note: one 2026 source lists private boats from 600,000–750,000 VND, so agree the price and boat size before boarding.
hours: Busiest 5:00–7:00; go by 5:30 at the latest. The market winds down by 9:00.
tip: The largest floating market in the Mekong Delta, and still a working wholesale market first and a tourist sight second. Each boat hangs its produce on a tall pole so buyers can see what it sells — look up, not just around. Hire your boat from Ninh Kieu Wharf (30 minutes' ride) or from Cai Rang itself. Eat breakfast from a boat: a bowl of noodle soup served on the water costs about 30,000–50,000 VND (~$1–2). Bring cash, a hat and sunscreen, and go on a weekday if you can — weekends are busier with tour boats.

name: Phong Dien Floating Market
address: Phong Dien District, about 20 km south-west of Can Tho city centre, Can Tho City
price: Not verified — boat hire similar to Cai Rang; agree the price before boarding
tip: Smaller and more local than Cai Rang, with fewer tour boats. Best combined with a bicycle ride through the orchard lanes of Phong Dien afterwards. Ask your hotel to arrange a boat the day before.

name: Son Islet (Con Son)
address: Son Islet, Can Tho River, Ninh Kieu District, Can Tho City
price: Not verified — ferry and community tour fees; check at the pier
tip: A community-run islet where local families welcome visitors into their orchards and fish farms — you can walk through fruit gardens, watch fish being fed, and eat lunch cooked by a family. It is a gentle, honest look at Delta life. Go with a local guide or ask your hotel to arrange the community tour.

name: Ben Tre — Coconut Canals
address: Ben Tre City, Ben Tre Province, about 2.5–3 hours by road from Can Tho City
price: Day-trip boat and car packages vary widely; agree the price with your hotel before you go. Sampan canal rides are typically included in a day tour of about 800,000–1,500,000 VND (~$31–58) per person — not verified at the counter.
hours: Daytime; start early to avoid the midday heat
tip: Ben Tre is the coconut capital of the Delta. The classic day is a boat on the wide river, then a hand-rowed sampan through narrow canals under coconut palms, with stops at a coconut candy workshop, a brick kiln and a family orchard. It is touristy in places and still lovely — the canal stretches are the quietest part. Most visitors do Ben Tre as a day trip from Ho Chi Minh City or from Can Tho; either way, go with a small group or a private boat if you can.

name: Chau Doc — Sam Mountain and Tra Su Cajuput Forest
address: Chau Doc City, An Giang Province, about 3 hours by road from Can Tho City, near the Cambodian border
price: Not verified — boat and entry fees; check at the counter
hours: Daytime; Tra Su forest is best in the morning (bird activity) and in the flood season, roughly September–November
tip: Chau Doc is the Delta's most distinctive town: floating fishing villages, Cham villages, Khmer pagodas and the sacred Sam Mountain, which locals climb for the view over the rice fields and the Cambodian border. Nearby Tra Su Cajuput Forest is a flooded forest you explore by boat, gliding through green duckweed under cajuput trees — one of the prettiest boat rides in the Delta. Chau Doc deserves an overnight stay, not a rushed day trip.

name: Can Tho Museum
address: 1 Hoa Binh Avenue, Ninh Kieu District, Can Tho City
price: Not verified — check at the counter
tip: A small, well-kept museum on the history and culture of the Delta — Khmer, Cham, Chinese and Vietnamese communities, river life and the wartime years. A good rainy-afternoon stop, and it helps everything else you see make sense.

name: Ninh Kieu Night Market
address: Hai Ba Trung Street, Ninh Kieu District, Can Tho City
price: Street snacks 20,000–60,000 VND (~$1–2)
tip: The evening counterpart to the floating market: grilled seafood, fruit shakes, clothes and souvenirs along the riverfront. Eat where locals are queuing.

name: Quan An Ngon Can Tho (local restaurant area, Ninh Kieu)
address: Not verified — please check on Google Maps
price: Mains roughly 50,000–150,000 VND (~$2–6)
tip: The Ninh Kieu riverfront is lined with local restaurants serving Delta dishes at local prices. Pick a busy one, point at what looks good, and order the grilled fish — it is usually the best thing on the menu.

name: Victoria Can Tho Resort
address: Cai Khe Ward, Ninh Kieu District, Can Tho City
price: High-end; roughly 2,000,000–4,000,000 VND (~$77–154) per night (check at booking)
tip: The city's classic riverside resort, with gardens, a pool and a restaurant on the river. Best for a splurge and for its sunset views over the Hau River.

name: Azerai Can Tho
address: Not verified — please check on Google Maps
price: High-end; roughly 3,000,000–6,000,000 VND (~$115–231) per night (check at booking)
tip: A quiet island resort a short boat ride from the city — you arrive by hotel boat, which sets the tone. Best for couples who want to switch off completely.

name: Kim Tho Hotel
address: Not verified — please check on Google Maps
price: Mid-range; roughly 600,000–1,200,000 VND (~$23–46) per night (check at booking)
tip: A solid mid-range choice in the centre, close to the wharf — ask the reception to arrange your floating market boat the evening before, so you only have to wake up and go.

name: Can Tho General Hospital
address: 21 Nguyen An Ninh Street, Ninh Kieu District, Can Tho City
price: Not verified
tip: The main public hospital in the city. For international-standard care, the nearest options are in Ho Chi Minh City, about 3–4 hours by road. Carry travel insurance that covers boat trips.

name: Tan An Market
address: 71 Hai Ba Trung Street, Tan An Ward, Ninh Kieu District, Can Tho City
price: Not verified — check at the stall; banh pia, dried fish and banh tet are all inexpensive market goods
tip: The oldest wholesale market in Can Tho and the gathering point for the Delta's specialties. Go in the morning for the fullest stalls, and bring cash.

name: Muoi Cuong Cacao Garden
address: 275 My Ai Hamlet, An Binh Ward, Can Tho City
price: Entry about 80,000 VND (~$3) per person including a drink; chocolate and cacao products priced in the shop — not verified
hours: Not verified — sources list 7:00 AM–12:00 PM and 8:00–11:00 AM
tip: A 1.2-hectare family cacao farm from the 1960s, about 12 km from the city centre. Check the current opening status before you go — one 2026 listing showed the farm as temporarily closed.

name: Sau Hoai Rice Noodle Factory
address: 476/14 Lo Vong Cung Street, An Binh Ward, Ninh Kieu District, Can Tho City
price: Entry about 5,000 VND (~$0.20) including a hands-on try; noodle pizza about 50,000 VND (~$2)
tip: Best reached by boat from Ninh Kieu Wharf as part of a Cai Rang floating market morning, or by motorbike along the canal road. Buy a pack of the coloured dried noodles — they travel well and cook in minutes.

name: Con Son Islet (Son Islet)
address: Con Son Islet, Hau River, Can Tho City
price: Not verified — homestay trips are quoted per trip; see Mekong Spirit for current rates
hours: Not verified — ferry and community tour fees and hours not verified
tip: A community-tourism islet of fruit gardens and fish farms, reached by a short ferry from the city. Go with a local guide or a homestay operator — the islet has no fixed sights, and the experience is the families you meet.

name: Phu Quoc International Airport
address: Phu Quoc International Airport, Duong To Commune, Phu Quoc, An Giang Province
price: Grab to Duong Dong around 180,000–220,000 VND (~$7–$9); metered taxi roughly 150,000–300,000 VND (~$6–$12)
tip: The airport has free Wi-Fi, currency exchange, and ATMs. Book your Grab after you collect your bags — drivers wait at the signed pickup point outside the terminal.

name: Bai Vong Port (ferry terminal)
